name: redef_elden_ring_d3d12_to_ipad_metal
rationale: This is the composite witness for the iPad target: the chain redef_framework_direct3d_12_to_cards + redef_d3d12_to_metal + redef_hlsl_to_msl + redef_framework_ios_sandbox_to_cards collectively makes ER's D3D12 render path expressible on iPad Metal. Each link in the chain is independently witnessed; this card asserts their composition is sound for the basic vertex+pixel pipeline, degrades gracefully for compute-heavy SM6.6 passes, and fails explicitly for cross-process resource sharing. The known failure modes are enumerated, not hidden. D3DMetal's existence on macOS demonstrates the approach is viable for AAA workloads; iPad inherits the same translation chain with tighter TDP/memory envelopes and a stricter app sandbox.

condition: Elden Ring's render loop and physics simulation are coupled at 60Hz. Naive FPS uncap (e.g. via driver vsync-off) accelerates physics: ladder climbs jump frames, Torrent's gallop speed changes, weapon-charge timings shift, and ragdoll behavior diverges from vanilla. Mods such as 'Elden Ring Reforged' and 'ER FPS Unlocker' decouple: physics runs at fixed 60Hz tick on a separate timer; render samples interpolated state at the panel's refresh rate. The redefinition admits a bit-identical physics trajectory for any input sequence between the source (vanilla 60fps) and the produced (uncapped render) variants — i.e. only the visual smoothness differs.

condition: Vanilla Elden Ring requires the player to traverse a fixed menu chain on every launch: title screen press-any-key, then a Continue/Load Game/New Game/Options menu, then a save-slot picker, before world streaming begins. The full chain consumes roughly 20 seconds of user interaction plus animation. The redefinition is a launcher flag that, when set, autopilots the menu chain by replaying the keystroke sequence (or by patching the menu state machine to enter the world directly with the last-used save slot). On Windows the launcher wraps the Steam shortcut; on Linux/Proton the launcher is a SteamTinkerLaunch profile that injects the autopilot before the EAC handshake. Identity is preserved by toggle: at fast_resume=false the menu chain is shown unchanged.

condition: Elden Ring has no native frame generation. The redefinition inserts interpolated frames between rendered frames via either (a) driver-level (AMD AFMF, NVIDIA Smooth Motion) or (b) game-level injection (Lukefz Universal FSR3, Optiscaler). Real fps_render is unchanged; presented fps_panel doubles or triples. Input latency rises by ~1 frame at the rendered rate (e.g. 40fps render → +25ms). Mouse/look input must still sample at render rate, not panel rate, to keep responsiveness; physics is unaffected because it runs on its own tick. Frame-gen is bit-identical on alternating frames to native render; interpolated frames are NOT bit-identical but are visually indistinguishable within the linear-motion regime.

condition: Vanilla Elden Ring caps render at a fixed 60fps regardless of power-source state, which is wasteful on a handheld where battery percentage and AC-power presence vary widely across a session. The redefinition replaces the static cap with a battery-aware curve that consults the Windows battery API (or vendor SDK) on a periodic tick and selects a framecap from a small table: e.g. 30fps below 20%, 40fps below 50%, 60fps on AC or above 50%. Physics still tick at the game's fixed simulation rate; the cap only governs render-loop frame budget, so the world simulation, animation cadence, and input timing are preserved. Identity case: when the device reports AC-connected and battery=100%, the curve selects 60fps and the render loop is bit-identical to vanilla. The redefinition reduces to vanilla on the trivial case, which is the soundness witness.

examples.note: identity: at full battery on AC the curve resolves to 60fps cap which is exactly the vanilla cap — the redefinition is the identity wrapper in this case.

condition: A handheld in undocked mode (small panel, battery, integrated gamepad) and a handheld docked to an external monitor with a wired controller have entirely different optimal settings: resolution, refresh rate, TDP envelope, framecap, and FSR2 mode all differ. Vanilla Elden Ring does not detect dock state and forces the user to alt-tab to Windows display settings on every transition. The redefinition installs a display-arrival/removal listener (SetupDi notifications, WM_DISPLAYCHANGE) and on each dock attach/detach event atomically swaps a profile bundle (render_resolution, framecap, tdp_target, fsr_mode) by calling into ER's runtime config or via a hook into the swap-chain creation path. The game's world state, save data, AI, and input bindings are untouched; only the GPU-side render-target, presentation chain, and TDP target are reconfigured. The swap is atomic: either all four parameters change on the same vsync boundary, or none do. Identity case: when no dock-state change event has fired since launch, the wrapper has never swapped a profile and runtime parameters equal vanilla.

examples.note: identity: with zero dock attach/detach events since process start, the wrapper has produced no profile swaps and the runtime config hash is identical to vanilla launch.

condition: Handheld panels have nonstandard native resolutions that diverge from desktop assumptions: ROG Ally and Ally X at 1920x1080 (Ally X at 120Hz), Legion Go at 2560x1600, Steam Deck LCD at 1280x800, Steam Deck OLED at 1280x800 with 90Hz. Vanilla Elden Ring exposes a fixed dropdown of presets and does not detect panel native, so users end up rendering at 1080p on a 1600p panel (blurry upscale) or at 1600p on a 7-inch panel (wasted GPU and battery). The redefinition queries the active display's EDID at launch, matches it against a small device table, and selects an internal render resolution that hits the FSR2 sweet spot for that panel (e.g. 1707x960 internal with FSR2 Quality output to 2560x1600, or native 1280x800 with FSR2 disabled on Deck). The pixel-accurate render path, post-processing chain, and asset LODs are unchanged; only the framebuffer dimensions and FSR2 input ratio are set. Identity case: when the detected panel reports 1920x1080 (the standard desktop preset ER ships with), the chosen resolution equals vanilla's default and rendering is bit-identical.

condition: Windows S0 modern-standby on handhelds (ROG Ally, Legion Go, MSI Claw) frequently re-enumerates HID devices on resume: the integrated gamepad disconnects during sleep and reattaches as a 'new' device, often with a different DirectInput/XInput slot. Vanilla Elden Ring locks its controller mapping at process start and does not rescan, so a resumed session shows the gamepad as disconnected or maps to an unbound slot, forcing the user to alt-tab through OS settings or restart the game. The redefinition is a thin wrapper that subscribes to Windows power-event broadcasts (PBT_APMRESUMESUSPEND, PBT_APMRESUMEAUTOMATIC) and to HID arrival events; on a sleep-resume cycle it re-resolves the integrated gamepad's vendor/product ID, re-applies the user's stored binding profile to ER's input layer within ~200ms, and emits no events when none are observed. The game's input semantics, deadzones, and binding values are unchanged; only the device handle is rebound. Identity case: when no sleep event has occurred since launch, the wrapper has never touched the input state and the binding table is bit-identical to vanilla.

examples.note: identity: with zero sleep-resume cycles since process start, the wrapper has produced zero rebind operations and the input-binding state hash equals vanilla launch state.

condition: On Windows handheld devices (ROG Ally, Legion Go, MSI Claw, Steam Deck running Windows), TDP (sustained Watts to the APU) is set globally or per-app via Armoury Crate SE, Legion Space, or third-party tools like HandheldCompanion. Vanilla Elden Ring has no concept of TDP and inherits whatever the user last configured at the OS level, leading to one-size-fits-all power draw whether the user is on battery in a cafe or docked at a desk. The redefinition wraps ER launch so that a per-game TDP profile is applied at process start and reverted at process exit, without the user opening Armoury Crate or Legion Space. Profiles are keyed by power-source state (e.g. 15W on battery, 25W on AC, 30W on dock) and pushed via the device-specific vendor service. Game frames, physics, audio, and inputs are untouched; only the APU power envelope changes, which indirectly affects achievable framerate but not the simulation. Identity case: when the user's selected profile matches the system default (no override applied), the wrapper is a no-op and ER runs exactly as it would without the wrapper.

examples.note: identity: when the per-game profile is set to 'system_default' the wrapper applies no override and the running TDP equals what the user already had configured at the OS level — byte-for-byte the same APU state as vanilla launch.

condition: Vanilla Elden Ring outputs SDR (BT.709, gamma 2.2, ~100 nits peak). The redefinition injects an HDR tonemap and color-space conversion at the swapchain, producing HDR10 (BT.2020 / PQ) or HDR400/HDR1000 output: SpecialK ReShade HDR on Windows desktop, gamescope HDR tonemap on Linux and Steam Deck OLED, or Windows 11 AutoHDR for handhelds running Windows. The injector intercepts the final SDR framebuffer, expands the dynamic range by inverting the SDR tonemap, lifts emissive surfaces (fire, lanterns, Erdtree glow) into the HDR highlight regime, and preserves SDR mid-tone luminance (~80-200 nits) so faces and stonework look identical to SDR. The bit-level invariant: at hdr_enabled == false (or panel reports SDR-only EDID), the injector passes the SDR buffer through untouched, so the swapchain output is byte-equal to vanilla. Game state, lighting calculations, and post-processing within the engine are untouched; only the final present is reinterpreted.

examples.note: identity: with HDR off (or an SDR-only panel) the injector is a pass-through; the swapchain bytes are byte-equal to vanilla SDR output.

condition: Composite optimal-launch redefinition for Elden Ring on the iPhone Pro 17 (A18 Pro chip, 6.3" ProMotion 120Hz OLED, 12GB RAM projected). The iPhone variant of the equivalent-of-GameMode profile for ER, recognising that iOS has no GameMode daemon, no nvidia-settings, no Proton — instead, the iOS substrate enforces equivalent optimizations through Apple-native APIs. Conditions: (1) Enable Metal HUD via MTLDevice.shouldShowHUD (debug-build only on App Store; sideloaded TrollStore builds can force it) — gives the ER frame-pacing telemetry the substrate needs; (2) Set max FPS = UIScreen.main.maximumFramesPerSecond (120 on iPhone 15 Pro / 17 Pro, 60 on standard iPhone) — substrate detects ProMotion and configures CADisplayLink.preferredFrameRateRange.maximum accordingly; (3) MetalShaderCacheLargestSize = 1G via MTLBinaryArchive serialized to NSCachesDirectory — sized to fit ER's full DXIL→MSL cross-compile cache without thrashing; (4) Use 60Hz lock for ER's 60fps cap (ER engine is hard-locked to 60 on consoles; substrate matches this via CADisplayLink.preferredFrameRateRange = {min: 60, max: 60, preferred: 60} even on a 120Hz panel — pacing variance is lower with a fixed-rate display link than with VRR on a 60fps-locked engine); (5) frame_gen = OFF (no DLSS-3 / FSR3 frame-generation on iPhone). The iPhone GPU thermal envelope (~6W sustained on Pro models, vs iPad Pro M4 ~20W and desktop dGPU 200W+) cannot sustain the additional compute for frame-interpolation; substrate forces frame_gen=off and falls back to MetalFX upscaling (2x spatial) instead. At identity case iphone_pro=false (standard iPhone, non-ProMotion), behaviour falls back to the 60Hz Metal pipeline unchanged — every condition above either no-ops or short-circuits to the 60Hz path. With ER_iPhone_target_active=false the substrate emits no Metal-HUD nor MetalShaderCache mutations and ER runs on whatever default Metal configuration the host shell installed.

examples.note: identity (no-op): with ER_iPhone_target_active=false on a standard non-Pro iPhone, substrate emits NO Metal/CADisplayLink/MTLBinaryArchive mutations; ER runs on whatever default Metal configuration the host shell installed. Establishes redefinition soundness at the no-op point. Both source and target collapse to vanilla_metal_default_pipeline.

no_gamemode_equivalent_daemon: iOS has no user-space daemon equivalent to Linux's gamemoded; performance/thermal hints are delivered via Apple Game Mode (iOS 18+) which is system-wide, not app-controllable. Substrate cannot pin the CPU governor or memory clock — Apple owns those decisions.

rationale: Tier-0 because ER on iPhone Pro 17 is the most-constrained Apple-Silicon target the substrate plans to emit for in W45. The 'GameMode equivalent' framing keeps parity with the Linux+NVIDIA 240Hz redef (redef_elden_ring_ubuntu_nvidia_240hz_gamemode_profile) so the substrate can reason about ER's launch experience across all three target families (Ubuntu+NV, iPad, iPhone) under a common composite-redefinition schema. condition: On Linux/Proton, DXVK translates Elden Ring's D3D11/D3D12 pipeline state into Vulkan pipelines and caches them in a per-prefix `.dxvk-cache` file. On a cold prefix every novel pipeline incurs a translation + Vulkan-compile cost, producing the well-known traversal stutter. The redefinition extends the universal shader_precompile_distribution card by additionally shipping a pre-warmed `.dxvk-cache` keyed to `(mesa_version, gpu_pci_id, dxvk_version)` and depositing it into the prefix before first launch. The bit-level invariant preserved is: rendered output for any given pipeline state object is identical whether the pipeline was JIT-compiled or loaded from the warmed cache; cache miss falls back to vanilla compile on the fly. When the distribution flag is off (deliver_cache=false), behavior reduces to vanilla DXVK cold-start. Pipeline identity is verified by the cache's internal SHA-1 of the DXBC + render-state tuple, so a mismatched cache simply misses and triggers normal compile.

examples.note: identity: with deliver_cache=false no warmed cache is written; DXVK starts cold exactly as vanilla Proton.
Pre-warmed cache eliminates first-encounter shader compilation stutter on the canonical opening traversal.

condition: Vanilla Elden Ring has no native HDR output path; the game renders to an RGBA8 SDR backbuffer and assumes a Rec.709/sRGB display transfer. Under Linux/Proton, gamescope can interpose between the game's swapchain and the compositor, intercepting the SDR backbuffer and applying an HDR tonemap (BT.2020 primaries, PQ EOTF) before scanout to an HDR10-capable panel. The redefinition extends the output pipeline with a tonemap stage gated on the hdr_enabled flag; when hdr_enabled is false the tonemap reduces to identity and the SDR pixels pass through unchanged. World-space rendering, lighting computation, and post-processing remain bit-identical to vanilla; only the final scanout transfer function is swapped. The bit-level invariant preserved is: linear-light scene radiance values are unchanged; only the encoding to display-referred values differs. Requires gamescope-session under SteamOS or `gamescope --hdr-enabled` wrapping the game, plus an HDR10-capable panel and a kernel/Mesa stack supporting HDR metadata.

examples.note: identity: with HDR disabled the gamescope tonemap stage is bypassed and the SDR backbuffer scans out unchanged; reduces to vanilla SDR output.
HDR enabled: gamescope tonemap maps SDR backbuffer to BT.2020/PQ; specular highlights on Erdtree leaves now exceed SDR 100-nit ceiling.

condition: Under Wayland compositors, Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) running inside Proton occasionally drops its online session when the surface loses focus due to alt-tab, monitor hot-plug, or workspace switching. The cause is that EAC's heartbeat socket is treated as session-bound and the compositor focus-change event is misinterpreted as a session termination signal by EAC's Windows-shim. The redefinition wraps EAC's runtime with a Wayland-aware shim that pins the heartbeat socket to the process lifetime rather than the surface lifetime, and discards xdg-shell `configure` and `activate` events from the EAC event loop. The bit-level invariant preserved is: every EAC anti-cheat measurement (memory scan, code-integrity hash, signed-input attestation) is computed identically; only the lifecycle of the network socket carrying those measurements is decoupled from compositor focus. With the shim disabled (focus_aware=true) behavior is identical to vanilla Proton EAC. No anti-cheat measurement is suppressed or modified.

condition: Multiple popular Elden Ring mods (Reforged, Convergence, Seamless Co-op, ERR-Hub, FOV mod, ResolutionUnlocker, SpecialK HDR) share a single hook chain through dinput8.dll and a single mod-folder layout under ModEngine2. When two mods both want to replace the same regulation.bin, override the same param row, or chain dinput8 hooks in conflicting orders, the result is a silent broken state: the game starts, but one mod's hooks never fire, params revert mid-session, or saves get cross-contaminated. The redefinition is a declarative manifest that names the chosen mod stack, pins each mod's version, declares the dinput8 chain order, declares the ModEngine2 mod-folder priority (alphabetical / explicit list), and validates that no two mods both claim exclusive ownership of the same regulation.bin row. A precheck step refuses to launch when the manifest detects a conflict. The bit-level invariant: when the manifest's mod_stack is the empty list, no dinput8.dll is placed in the game directory, no ModEngine2 launcher is used, and the game launches vanilla; ER0000.sl2 writes are byte-equal to an unmodded session with the same inputs.

condition: Even when Elden Ring achieves a stable average FPS, frame-to-frame present intervals are bursty: a 60fps average can include 8ms and 25ms frames alternating, perceived as judder. The redefinition routes presents through a pacing layer: on Linux gamescope adds a present-time scheduler; on Windows SpecialK or the Xbox Game Bar GPU scheduler enforces minimum-variance present intervals. Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) combined with present-pacing is the complete fix: VRR matches panel to render rate, pacing matches render rate to physics tick, physics tick is fixed at 60Hz. The redefinition is bit-identical in rendered frames; only present time is reshaped.

examples.note: identity: rendered frame pixels are bit-identical between vanilla and paced — present-pacing only reshapes WHEN frames appear, not WHAT they contain.

condition: Vanilla Elden Ring stores all save data in opaque binary blobs: ER0000.sl2 (local save, 10 character slots packed with checksums and obfuscation), ER0000.co2 (steam cloud backup), and a per-Steam-ID directory under the platform's user save root. The vanilla launcher offers no way to view slot summaries, back up before risky decisions, branch a save for experimentation, or recover from a corruption. The redefinition layers a UI wrapper that parses the .sl2 container, extracts per-slot metadata (character name, level, runes held, time played, last grace site, build hash), and exposes operations: backup (copy .sl2 to timestamped archive), restore (atomic write-with-checksum), branch (duplicate slot N into slot M of a sibling .sl2), and diff (compare two saves' character stats). The bit-level invariant: when no save-management action is taken (UI is read-only or closed), the underlying ER0000.sl2 and ER0000.co2 bytes are bit-identical to vanilla. Reads parse via a memory-mapped view without writing; writes only occur on explicit user action and produce a new .sl2 that round-trips through the vanilla loader.

condition: Elden Ring uses DirectX 12 PSO (Pipeline State Object) compilation on first encounter of each shader permutation. The first visit to Limgrave, Stormveil, Caelid etc. triggers 1-3 second hitches as the driver compiles ~200-400 PSOs. Under Proton/DXVK on Linux the equivalent is DXVK state-cache compilation. Cache hits produce bit-identical pipeline output; the redefinition is purely a build-time vs run-time tradeoff.

condition: Elden Ring caps internally at 60 fps (engine-side; bypassing it via er_fps_unlocker is out of scope for this card). On a 240Hz panel, a fixed 60fps source presents as one rendered frame per four panel scans. Without VRR, this either tears (vsync off) or stutters at the 16.67ms / 4.17ms beat mismatch. The 240Hz VRR + LFC profile rebuilds the present path so ER's vanilla 60fps source is smooth on a 240Hz panel: (1) the panel must be VESA Adaptive-Sync / G-SYNC Compatible capable (vrr_capable_panel_driver card); (2) nvidia-settings CurrentMetaMode must include {AllowGSYNCCompatible=On} on the panel's connector; (3) the panel's VRR range is typically 48-240Hz — below 48Hz the panel hardware cannot vary refresh; (4) ER's 60fps source sits ABOVE the VRR lower bound, so per-frame VRR negotiation works natively for 60fps content without LFC; (5) Low-Framerate Compensation (LFC) is enabled as a safety net for the case where ER drops below 48fps (heavy boss-arena particles, mid-area transitions) — LFC doubles the present rate to keep the panel inside its VRR window (e.g. a 40fps drop is presented as 80Hz panel scan). The bit-level invariant: at steady-state 60fps in ER, the panel runs at 60Hz refresh (or 120Hz under LFC doubling, depending on driver implementation) with each rendered frame held for exactly one panel scan; no tearing, no judder at the 60-vs-240 beat mismatch. At panel_hz==60 (the VRR window collapses to a single rate equal to ER's source rate), behavior is identical to vanilla 60Hz fixed-refresh — the redefinition is sound at that identity point.

examples.note: identity: at a fixed 60Hz panel (no VRR, panel native = ER source rate), there is no beat-mismatch and no LFC need; substrate behavior == vanilla 60Hz fixed-refresh. Establishes redefinition soundness at the degenerate panel point.

ER's vanilla 60fps source sits inside the panel's 48-240Hz VRR range, so each rendered frame triggers a panel refresh per-frame (panel scans at 60Hz). The composition is comp_cf_if(fps >= vrr_lower_bound, comp_cf_call(per_frame_vrr_present), comp_cf_call(lfc_double_present)).

examples.target_eval: VRR+LFC active: panel refreshes at 60Hz to match ER's 60fps source; no beat-mismatch, no judder

condition: Composite optimal-launch profile for Elden Ring on the Ubuntu + AMD CPU + NVIDIA GPU + 240Hz panel + GameMode stack. The profile is a frozen tuple of launch-time settings that, when all true, yield a reproducible best-case ER launch on this hardware. Conditions: (1) Steam launch options begin with 'gamemoderun %command%' so the GameMode daemon raises cpufreq governor to performance and the IO priority bias takes effect; (2) nvidia-settings -a '[gpu:0]/GPUPowerMizerMode=1' (PowerMizer = Prefer Maximum Performance) — pins the NVIDIA GPU to its highest P-state so the first-minute clock-ramp stutter on ER's intro doesn't happen; (3) kernel cmdline includes nvidia_drm.modeset=1 — required for any DRM kms client (gamescope, kwin/mutter compositor wayland surface) to negotiate flip-presents with the NVIDIA driver; (4) nvidia-settings CurrentMetaMode includes {AllowGSYNCCompatible=On} on the panel's DisplayPort connector (DP-1 in the canonical layout) — enables G-SYNC Compatible / VESA Adaptive-Sync at the connector level; (5) Proton-GE 9-20 or newer is pinned in Steam's compatibility tool selector — guards against silent Proton-Experimental regressions in the EAC / vkd3d-proton stack; (6) DXVK_FRAME_RATE=240 (or uncapped via empty value) in the launch env — prevents DXVK from applying its default frame-pacing throttle below the panel rate; (7) VKD3D_CONFIG=dxr11 — enables vkd3d-proton's DXR 1.1 path so ER's ray-tracing toggle works on supported NVIDIA cards; (8) CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 — pins the NVIDIA dGPU as the rendering device, defending against Optimus-style mis-selection on hybrid laptop layouts. The profile is COMPOSITE: each leaf is enforced by the corresponding leaf framework's redefinition (redef_framework_gamemode_to_cards, redef_framework_nvidia_settings_to_cards, redef_framework_vkd3d_proton_to_cards, redef_framework_proton_ge_custom_to_cards). With profile_active=false, the substrate emits no launch-env mutations and behavior equals vanilla Proton default.

condition: Vanilla Elden Ring renders at a fixed 16:9 aspect ratio; on 21:9 and 32:9 displays the engine either pillarboxes (black bars) or horizontally stretches the framebuffer and HUD, distorting circles and text. The redefinition reprojects the view frustum to the true display aspect using a Hor+ FOV scaling convention (vertical FOV preserved, horizontal FOV expanded), repositions HUD elements (compass, health/stamina bars, item prompts) into the central 16:9 safe zone of the wider canvas, and removes the engine's cinematic black-bar overlays so cutscenes fill the panel without stretching. Mods such as Flawless Widescreen's Elden Ring profile and ResolutionUnlocker patch the renderer to honor the desktop resolution and reproject UI quads. The bit-level invariant: at aspect_ratio == 16:9 the redefinition is a no-op, so the rendered framebuffer, HUD layout, and cutscene letterboxing are byte-equal to vanilla. Physics, save data, and shader output for the original frustum remain unchanged. Wider aspects only add pixels to the horizontal edges; the original 16:9 center region is bit-identical to the vanilla render.

condition: OBSERVATION-REFERENCE card (W46 pivot). Capstone is no longer invoked as a runtime dependency. The substrate OBSERVED Capstone's open source code (BSD-3) to DERIVE the shape of card-native ISA decoding primitives at cards/isa/x86_64/ and cards/isa/arm64/ (and cards/isa/rv32i/). Capstone's three externally-observable primitives (cs_open, cs_disasm, cs_close) informed the card-native decode pipeline shape: arch_dispatch_card → per-instruction decode fold → instruction-record stream. At runtime, the substrate executes the derived card-native primitives via substrate-native ISA decoders (per-architecture cards/isa/<arch>/<MNEMONIC>/ entries plus a substrate-native decode-fold executor) — NOT via libcapstone.so. This card documents the derivation evidence: Capstone source patterns were the source for the dispatch shape; the actual per-byte→mnemonic decoding is realized by the cards/isa/ corpus, not by linking against Capstone.

examples.note: identity (L34 anchor): at empty_bytes, Capstone's cs_disasm yields the empty instruction list; the derived card-native fold over zero bytes also yields the empty list (no comp_cf_call(decode_one_card, ...) nodes emitted). External no-op == derived no-op.

observation evidence: Capstone's arch/X86/ subdir contains the (arch, mode) → decoder table dispatch. This informed the card-native primitive shape: comp_cf_call(arch_dispatch_card, [arch, mode]) selects which cards/isa/x86_64/ card-set the downstream decode fold consults. Runtime is now the substrate-native isa corpus, not libcapstone.

For bytes 48 89 c3, Capstone's x86_64 decoder produces 'mov rbx, rax' — the derived card-native equivalent emits an observed_instruction record referencing cards/isa/x86_64/MOV/card.json (canonical_bytes='48 89 c3').

condition: Apple's codesign CLI exposes four externally-observable primitives: (1) codesign_sign applies a signature blob to a target (Mach-O binary or .app bundle), embedding a SuperBlob in the LC_CODE_SIGNATURE load command and writing _CodeSignature/CodeResources for bundles; (2) codesign_verify recomputes the file-hash manifest and validates it against the embedded signature + the certificate chain; (3) codesign_display_requirements prints the designated requirement (DR) baked into a signature; (4) codesign_remove_signature strips an existing signature. L62 requires these to map to card-native primitives. The redefinition: codesign_sign -> comp_cf_if(identity_in_keychain, comp_cf_call(emit_signature_blob, [target, identity, entitlements]), comp_cf_call(refuse_no_identity, [])); the emit_signature_blob is itself a fold (comp_ds_list_cons) over the file-tree producing per-file sha256 entries (the CodeResources files dict). codesign_verify -> comp_cf_call(recompute_manifest_card, [target]) followed by comp_cf_if(observed_hashes == stored_hashes && cert_chain_valid, comp_cf_call(return_ok), comp_cf_call(return_verify_failure)). codesign_display_requirements -> comp_ds_record_get(signature_record, 'designated_requirement'). codesign_remove_signature -> comp_cf_if(target_has_signature, comp_cf_call(strip_lc_code_signature), comp_cf_call(noop)). The redefinition is BEHAVIORAL: the actual cryptographic primitives (CMS-wrap of the CodeDirectory, sha256 chain) live behind deferred crypto cards; substrate-observed semantics are the orchestration layer above them.

identity present: signing emits the SuperBlob + writes _CodeSignature/CodeResources. The redefinition decomposes this into a comp_ds_list_cons fold over the file tree (producing per-file sha256 entries) followed by a comp_cf_call to the deferred CMS-wrap primitive. Behavior-equivalent at the file-manifest level; CMS-wrap is the honest gap.

name: redef_framework_codesign_to_cards
rationale: Demonstrates L62 on codesign. Each CLI primitive is naturally a comp_cf_call wrapped by comp_cf_if (identity-existence guard for sign; signature-existence guard for verify/remove); the per-file CodeResources manifest is a comp_ds_list_cons fold over the .app file tree. condition: D3DMetal is Apple's DirectX-to-Metal translation layer (Game Porting Toolkit). L62 requires these to map to card-native primitives. The redefinition: d3d_to_metal_command_translation -> comp_cf_call(d3d_to_metal_dispatch_card, [d3d_fn_id, args]) — identity-transform at the lookup level (the dispatch card encodes the static translation table); hlsl_to_msl_shader_translation -> comp_cf_call(dxbc_or_dxil_to_msl_card, [shader_blob]) — declared gap until the compile category exists; dxgi_swapchain_to_metal_drawable -> comp_ds_pair(input_back_buffer_texture, output_metal_drawable) — the swap-chain is fundamentally an input/output buffer pair across the D3D → Metal boundary. condition: Direct3D 12 is redefined DIRECTLY to the card-native graphics_api primitive set (cards/computation/graphics_api/comp_gfx_*) — not via DXVK, not via VKD3D-Proton, not via D3DMetal. The 14 card-native graphics_api primitives form a target-agnostic explicit-GPU command-buffer model (device + queue + buffer + texture + resource_destroy + shader_module + pipeline_state + command_buffer_begin/end + cmd_set_pipeline + cmd_bind_resources + cmd_draw + cmd_dispatch + submit_and_present); every D3D12 COM call resolves to a sequence over this set. Mapping pattern: object-creation primitives (D3D12CreateDevice, CreateCommandQueue, CreateCommittedResource, CreateRootSignature, CreatePipelineState, CreateDescriptorHeap, CreateSwapChain) map to comp_gfx_device_create / comp_gfx_command_queue_create / comp_gfx_buffer_create or comp_gfx_texture_create / comp_gfx_pipeline_state_create; command-recording primitives (SetPipelineState, SetGraphicsRootSignature, IASetVertexBuffers, DrawInstanced, Dispatch, CopyResource) map to comp_gfx_command_buffer_begin then a sequence of comp_gfx_cmd_* opcodes then comp_gfx_command_buffer_end; submission/present (ExecuteCommandLists + IDXGISwapChain::Present) map to comp_gfx_submit_and_present. DXVK and VKD3D-Proton are now OBSERVATION SOURCES used to validate the mapping correctness (their per-call decomposition is a useful sanity reference) — they are NOT RUNTIME DEPENDENCIES. The actual runtime backends are vulkan_backend_executor (Linux/Ubuntu/Windows-via-Vulkan) and metal_backend_executor (iOS/macOS), each of which implements the 14 comp_gfx_* primitives natively against its target GPU API. The redefinition is therefore backend-agnostic: the same comp_gfx_* sequence runs against any executor that honors the primitive contracts.

examples.note: identity: at d3d12_call == noop (an empty D3D12 command list with no recorded opcodes, executed against an empty queue), the redefinition produces an empty graph over comp_gfx_*; the substrate behavior collapses to the native no-op. Both the source D3D12 path and the target card-native graph produce the same observable side-effect (none). source_eval and target_eval string-equal — establishes L34 soundness at the identity point.

device creation maps DIRECTLY to comp_gfx_device_create. The D3D12 adapter index becomes the card-native adapter_index parameter; feature_level is captured as device-side capability metadata (queryable via the device handle but not part of the create signature itself). No DXVK, no VKD3D — the executor (vulkan_backend_executor on Linux, metal_backend_executor on iOS/macOS) realizes comp_gfx_device_create against its target API.

name: redef_framework_direct3d_12_to_cards
rationale: Architectural pivot (W46): Direct3D 12 is redefined DIRECTLY onto the card-native graphics_api primitive set (14 comp_gfx_* primitives), making the redefinition target-agnostic and substrate-pure. Previous form wrapped D3D12 over comp_cf_call against DXVK/VKD3D — that tied the substrate's runtime to DXVK as a dependency, which is wrong: per universal-transferability the substrate must speak in card-native primitives, not in third-party translation-layer wrappers. The new form treats DXVK and VKD3D-Proton as observation sources for correctness validation only (their per-call decomposition is a useful cross-reference for the mapping); the actual runtime is whichever card-native backend executor is loaded at the target — vulkan_backend_executor on Linux/Ubuntu/Windows-via-Vulkan, metal_backend_executor on iOS/macOS/iPad. The same card-native command graph thus runs everywhere comp_gfx_* is implemented.

condition: OBSERVATION-REFERENCE card (W46 pivot). DXVK is no longer invoked as a runtime dependency by the substrate. Instead, the substrate OBSERVED DXVK's open source code to DERIVE the shape of card-native graphics_api primitives. DXVK's three externally-observable primitives (translate_d3d_call, manage_state_cache, shader_compile) informed the card-native equivalents at cards/computation/graphics_api/ (command-buffer recording + pipeline state) and cards/computation/shader_lang/ (DXBC/DXIL→SPIR-V translation). At runtime, the substrate executes the derived card-native primitives via substrate-native backend executors (tool_vulkan_backend_executor, tool_metal_backend_executor) — NOT via DXVK. This card documents the derivation evidence: which DXVK source patterns produced which card-native primitive shapes. The runtime role DXVK USED to fulfill is now fulfilled by substrate-native Vulkan/Metal backend executors, ensuring universal transferability across non-Linux platforms.

condition: OBSERVATION-REFERENCE card (W46 / W47 pivot). Frida is not invoked as a hard runtime dependency. The substrate OBSERVED Frida's Python binding + frida-core source to DERIVE the shape of card-native runtime-trace primitives (process-attach, hook-install, message-channel ingest). At runtime, the substrate's live_runtime_tracer tool calls into frida-the-library WHEN AVAILABLE, but the card-native model of what each Frida primitive does is fully expressed below in comp_sys_* + comp_io_stream_* + comp_cf_call terms. When Frida is absent, the tool falls back to spec-mode which executes the same card-native shape but synthesizes deterministic events instead of attaching to a real process.

examples.note: identity (L34 anchor): attach with pid=0 is conventionally the current process. Frida's behavior is to inject the agent into its own address space; the card-native equivalent is comp_sys_memory_map for the agent page + comp_sys_thread_spawn for the agent thread, both in the same address space — observationally a degenerate attach.

observation evidence: Frida's attach(pid) injects frida-agent into the target's address space via ptrace(Linux), mach_inject(macOS), or CreateRemoteThread(Windows). The card-native shape models this as a comp_sys_memory_map (the agent page in the target VMA) followed by comp_sys_thread_spawn (the agent thread running the JS engine). The Session handle becomes a comp_io_stream pair (rx + tx) over which message envelopes flow.

Each send() in JS becomes one comp_io_stream_write in the agent + one comp_io_stream_read in the controller. The Python on('message', cb) is the controller-side dispatch.

condition: iOS sandbox is the kernel-enforced restriction profile on every third-party app. It exposes four externally-observable primitives that gate normal Darwin behavior: (1) fs_access_guarded — open(2) on out-of-container paths returns EPERM; (2) no_jit_rwx — mmap with PROT_RWX returns EPERM unless the process holds com.apple.developer.cs.allow-jit; (3) app_group_only_filesystem — cross-app sharing only via group.<bundle> containers; (4) no_arbitrary_fork — fork(2)/vfork(2)/posix_spawn(3) return EPERM from third-party processes. L62 requires these guards to map to card-native primitives. The redefinition: each guard is a comp_cf_if predicate (sandbox_allows_path / has_jit_entitlement / path_in_app_group / process_is_system) wrapped around a comp_cf_call to the underlying Darwin primitive — when the predicate is true the call proceeds, when false it returns EPERM. The identity case is: with sandbox_active=false (jailbroken or developer mode), every guard's predicate evaluates true and the redefinition reduces to the macOS-equivalent call. This makes the iOS-vs-macOS delta surface as a single conditional: the substrate can reason about ER-on-iPad by composing the macOS redefinitions with the four sandbox guards.

examples.note: identity: with sandbox_active=false, all four guards' predicates evaluate true and the redefinition reduces to the macOS-equivalent calls — substrate behavior == macos_native. Establishes redefinition soundness at the disabled-sandbox point.

condition: ldid is the open-source equivalent of codesign for the iOS sideload + jailbreak workflow. It exposes four externally-observable primitives: (1) ldid_sign_adhoc applies an ad-hoc (self-signed) signature to a Mach-O via `ldid -S[entitlements.plist]`; (2) ldid_sign_with_p12 applies a CA-chained signature using a PKCS#12 keystore via `ldid -K<keystore.p12>`; (3) ldid_inspect_signature dumps the existing signature blob (`ldid -e` for entitlements, `ldid -h` for the SuperBlob); (4) ldid_remove_signature strips a signature via `ldid -r`. L62 requires these to map to card-native primitives. The redefinition: ldid_sign_adhoc -> comp_cf_call(emit_adhoc_signature, [target, entitlements]) where emit_adhoc_signature = fold(comp_ds_list_cons, sha256(per_file)) + deferred SuperBlob-emit (no CMS wrap needed for ad-hoc, which is the structural difference from codesign). ldid_sign_with_p12 -> comp_cf_if(p12_decrypts_with_passphrase, comp_cf_call(emit_p12_signature, [target, p12, entitlements]), comp_cf_call(refuse_bad_passphrase, [])). ldid_inspect_signature -> comp_ds_record_get(signature_record, 'entitlements' | 'superblob_index'). ldid_remove_signature -> comp_cf_if(target_has_signature, comp_cf_call(strip_signature_blob), comp_cf_call(noop)). The redefinition is BEHAVIORAL but, unlike codesign, ldid's source code is open (AGPL-3.0), so the derivation has direct access to the SuperBlob byte layout -- the substrate's lifting plan derives the substrate-native SuperBlob emitter from ldid's source.

condition: Apple Metal exposes eight externally-observable primitives: MTLDevice (device handle), MTLCommandQueue (FIFO submission queue), MTLCommandBuffer (recordable container), MTLRenderPipelineState + MTLComputePipelineState (immutable compiled PSOs), MTLBuffer + MTLTexture (GPU memory handles), MTLLibrary (compiled shader module). L62 requires these to map to card-native primitives. The redefinition: device/queue/buffer/texture handle acquisition all reduce to comp_cf_call against the device factory function (each handle is the call's return value); MTLCommandBuffer.commit() is a comp_cf_call that schedules asynchronous GPU execution; PSO + shader-function lookups inside an encoder reduce to comp_ds_record_get over a compiled pipeline-state record indexed by descriptor key. The redefinition is BEHAVIORAL — substrate cannot reproduce Apple's internal Metal driver, AIR codegen, or chip-specific bytecode emission — but it declaratively expresses the visible call surface so downstream redefinitions (ER-on-macOS, ER-on-iPad) can be reasoned about in card-native vocabulary.

condition: Seamless Co-op is an open-world co-op mod for Elden Ring (replaces FromSoftware's instanced summon co-op). It exposes four externally-observable primitives: (1) replicate_state_across_clients — push player position/inventory/quest-flags as a stream of state deltas to peer clients; (2) bypass_eac_for_modded_session — custom auth handshake that allows modded clients to connect without EAC interference; (3) persistent_companion_logic — keep companion-player loaded across area transitions (vanilla unloads them); (4) shared_world_events — replicate world-state mutations (boss kills, lever pulls, NPC kills) to all peers. L62 requires these to map to card-native primitives. The redefinition: replicate_state_across_clients -> queue of state-deltas built via comp_ds_list_cons, dispatched via comp_cf_call(net_send_card); bypass_eac_for_modded_session -> comp_cf_if(handshake_valid, comp_cf_call(allow_connect_card), comp_cf_call(reject_card)); persistent_companion_logic -> comp_cf_if(area_transition, comp_cf_call(retain_companion_card), comp_cf_call(default_unload_card)); shared_world_events -> comp_cf_call(broadcast_event_card, [event]) + comp_ds_list_cons to event-queue. Behavioral redefinition — the mod's actual auth-bypass internals are not reproducible by the substrate (and would be inappropriate to reproduce); substrate declares what each primitive does in card-native vocabulary.

condition: UIKit's device-class detection surface is the externally-observable subset of UIDevice + UITraitCollection that the substrate uses to dispatch between iPhone and iPad code paths at runtime. The framework exposes five primitives the substrate cares about: (1) UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom — returns UIUserInterfaceIdiomPhone | Pad | Mac | TV | CarPlay | Vision | Unspecified; (2) UIDevice.current.model — string descriptor like 'iPhone' / 'iPad'; (3) UIScreen.main.nativeBounds — pixel rect of the built-in display; (4) UIScreen.main.maximumFramesPerSecond — 60 or 120 (ProMotion); (5) UITraitCollection.userInterfaceIdiom — the trait-collection-scoped idiom (matches UIDevice but is observable inside SwiftUI Environment). L62 requires this framework's primitives to map to card-native primitives in cards/computation/. The redefinition: each query becomes a comp_cf_if (idiom branch) wrapping a comp_cf_call (record lookup) parameterised by a comp_ds_record_get against a per-device trait record. UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom -> comp_cf_if(idiom == phone, comp_cf_call(iphone_branch), comp_cf_if(idiom == pad, comp_cf_call(ipad_branch), comp_cf_call(default_branch))). The redefinition is BEHAVIORAL: actual UIKit C API calls live inside Apple's framework binary; substrate validates observable I/O equivalence (given the same idiom, same record lookup, same branch). The identity case is: at userInterfaceIdiom=unknown, behavior == iPad-default — the substrate's fallback when it cannot identify the device class is to assume iPad ergonomics (larger / more permissive layout), because a too-small touch target on a too-small screen is worse than slightly-too-large on a larger one.

examples.note: identity: with userInterfaceIdiom=unknown (substrate has no mapping for the device model), redefinition falls through to iPad-default behavior — substrate behavior == ipad_default_layout_and_profile. Establishes redefinition soundness at the no-idiom-detected fallback point. Both source and target collapse to ipad_default_layout_and_profile.
iPhone idiom: predicate (idiom == phone) evaluates true; substrate dispatches the iphone_branch. Behavior-equivalent to switching on UIUserInterfaceIdiomPhone in a Swift Cocoa Touch app.

iPad idiom: predicate (idiom == pad) evaluates true; substrate dispatches the ipad_branch. Maps to comp_cf_if(comp_ds_record_get(device_traits, 'idiom') == 'pad', comp_cf_call(load_ipad_layout, []), comp_cf_call(fall_through_to_default, [])).

Mac Catalyst idiom: substrate dispatches the mac_branch (use AppKit-style input rather than touch). Maps to comp_cf_if(comp_ds_record_get(device_traits, 'idiom') == 'mac', comp_cf_call(load_macos_layout, []), comp_cf_call(fall_through_to_pad, [])).

Trait-collection-scoped idiom query (SwiftUI Environment): observed via UITraitCollection.current.userInterfaceIdiom. Substrate maps this to the SAME record-lookup as the UIDevice query because both should agree at runtime; if they diverge (multi-window scene with adapted traits), substrate prefers the trait-collection answer because it reflects the current scene's effective idiom.

flaws: redefines_a_synthetic_framework: UIKit's device-class detection subset is not a free-standing framework binary — it is a small surface inside UIKit.framework (UIDevice + UITraitCollection classes). This redefinition card binds to that subset for L62 redefinition accounting; the full UIKit surface (views, controls, layout) is out of scope here.

idiom_strings_apple_owned: UIUserInterfaceIdiom enum values are Apple-defined integers; substrate cannot guarantee forward compatibility if Apple adds a new idiom (e.g. .reality on visionOS 3+). The unknown-idiom fallback to iPad-default mitigates but doesn't eliminate.

trait_vs_device_can_diverge: in iPad multi-window scenarios with adapted UITraitCollection (e.g. a window sized to phone-width), UITraitCollection.userInterfaceIdiom can return .phone while UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom returns .pad. Substrate prefers trait-scoped answer but the divergence path is not fully modeled.

no_runtime_introspect_card_yet: comp_runtime_introspect_device + comp_trait_collection_observe are deferred; the redefinition currently relies on comp_ds_record_get against a synthesized device_traits record, but the upstream pipeline that populates that record from UIKit calls is not yet card-native.

Path to observation-derived: instrument a real iPhone + iPad launch via Xcode runtime + Frida script logging every UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom and UITraitCollection.current.userInterfaceIdiom call, capture the actual idiom resolutions, and machine-derive the redefinition's predicate set. The hand-authored card is a hypothesis to validate.

The identity at userInterfaceIdiom=unknown (== iPad-default) is the substrate's gate for proving 'on an unknown device class, fall through to the iPad-default touch layout', which is the lifting plan for unmapped UIDevice.model strings (new iPhone generations, future Apple form factors before substrate updates).

name: redef_framework_vulkan_to_cards
rationale: Demonstrates the L62 pattern on the substrate's PRIMARY graphics target. Unlike DXVK/VKD3D-Proton (which translate D3D -> Vulkan), Vulkan IS the destination of the substrate's graphics_api IR; the redefinition is therefore largely identity (1:1 primitive mappings). The empty-command-buffer case (no recorded vkCmd*) corresponds to the empty card-native graphics graph, anchoring L41 non-vacuously at the no-op point. This is the L62 spine for the W46 card-native pivot: substrate-emitted graphics no longer flow through DXVK/VKD3D-Proton; they are consumed natively by vulkan_backend_executor against this redefinition.

condition: HLSL is Microsoft's shading language compiled to DXBC (Shader Model 5.x) or DXIL (Shader Model 6.x); MSL is Apple's Metal Shading Language compiled to AIR. The redefinition expresses HLSL/DXIL primitives -> MSL primitives translation, the per-shader-stage path inside redef_d3d12_to_metal. The canonical toolchain is dxc + spirv-cross (DXIL -> SPIR-V -> MSL) but a direct DXIL -> MSL backend exists in D3DMetal and in commercial cross-compilers (Apple's open-sourced spirv-cross fork, Khronos's reference). Many HLSL primitives are syntactically near-identical to MSL: arithmetic, vector swizzles, matrix multiplication, intrinsics like dot/cross/normalize/saturate. The non-trivial gaps are: cbuffer -> Metal argument-buffer layout; Texture2D.Sample -> texture.sample with explicit sampler binding; SV_ semantics -> [[attribute]] / [[position]] / [[stage_in]]; HLSL register(t0/s0/b0) -> Metal [[texture(0)]] / [[sampler(0)]] / [[buffer(0)]]; UAV memory model (RWBuffer/RWTexture) -> Metal access::read_write textures and atomic buffers; wave/lane intrinsics (WaveActiveBallot, QuadReadAcross) -> Metal simdgroup_ballot/quad_broadcast.

examples.note: identity: empty shader (just main with no body / passthrough vertex shader) translates to an empty function with the same signature shape. The translation reduces to a syntactic shell when there is no per-instruction work to do — both HLSL and MSL forms compile to an empty AIR/DXIL body, so their semantic evaluation is the same no-op. Establishes redefinition soundness at the empty-input case.
scalar/vector arithmetic is syntactically identical between HLSL and MSL — both inherit C-family operator syntax for float ops. comp_numeric_binop maps directly across.
examples.source_eval: HLSL: float c = a + b;  // compiles to DXIL fadd float
examples.target_eval: MSL:  float c = a + b;  // compiles to AIR fadd float. comp_numeric_binop(add, a, b, float)

input.hlsl_decl: cbuffer SceneConstants : register(b0) { float4x4 view; float4x4 proj; }

examples.note: cbuffer in HLSL becomes a Metal argument buffer or [[buffer(n)]] struct in MSL. Layout (row-major vs column-major) and packing rules differ; HLSL default column-major must be respected. Field access via comp_ds_record_get.
examples.source_eval: HLSL: cbuffer SceneConstants : register(b0) { float4x4 view; float4x4 proj; }; matrix m = view * proj;
examples.target_eval: MSL: struct SceneConstants { float4x4 view; float4x4 proj; }; ...(constant SceneConstants& cb [[buffer(0)]])... float4x4 m = cb.view * cb.proj; comp_cf_call(emit_msl_cbuffer, [comp_ds_record_get(hlsl_decl, 'fields'), comp_ds_record_get(hlsl_decl, 'register_slot')])

examples.note: Texture2D.Sample becomes texture.sample with explicit sampler binding. HLSL register(t0)/register(s0) become MSL [[texture(0)]]/[[sampler(0)]]. This is the most common per-pixel primitive in ER's gbuffer/lighting passes.
examples.source_eval: HLSL: Texture2D tex : register(t0); SamplerState samp : register(s0); float4 c = tex.Sample(samp, uv);
examples.target_eval: MSL: texture2d<float> tex [[texture(0)]], sampler samp [[sampler(0)]]; float4 c = tex.sample(samp, uv); comp_cf_call(emit_msl_texture_sample, [comp_ds_pair('tex', 'samp'), 'uv'])

input.hlsl_decl: struct VSOut { float4 pos : SV_Position; float3 nrm : NORMAL; };

examples.note: SV_Position / NORMAL / TEXCOORD HLSL semantics translate to MSL [[position]] / [[user(...)]] / explicit attributes via MTLVertexDescriptor. The per-field semantic must be remapped at struct-emission time.
examples.source_eval: HLSL: struct VSOut { float4 pos : SV_Position; float3 nrm : NORMAL; };
examples.target_eval: MSL: struct VSOut { float4 pos [[position]]; float3 nrm [[user(NORMAL)]]; }; comp_cf_call(emit_msl_struct_with_semantics, [comp_ds_record_get(hlsl_decl, 'fields')])

examples.note: most HLSL intrinsics map 1:1 to MSL with minor renames: lerp -> mix, mad -> fma (or a*b+c), rsqrt -> rsqrt, saturate -> saturate (identical), step -> step (identical). A small rename table covers the bulk.
examples.target_eval: MSL: float r = mix(a, b, 0.5); comp_cf_call(rename_intrinsic, [comp_ds_record_get(intrinsic, 'name'), 'hlsl_to_msl'])

examples.note: wave intrinsics (SM6.0+) translate to simdgroup intrinsics in MSL. WaveActiveBallot -> simd_ballot; QuadReadAcrossX -> quad_shuffle; lane size differs (HLSL wave=32/64 driver-dependent, MSL simdgroup=32 on Apple GPUs). Some HLSL intrinsics have no MSL equivalent and require fallback.
examples.target_eval: MSL: simd_vote ballot = simd_ballot(thread_should_participate); comp_cf_if(intrinsic_has_msl_equivalent, comp_cf_call(emit_msl_simdgroup_intrinsic, [name]), comp_cf_call(emit_msl_fallback_loop, [name]))

flaws: sm66_feature_gap: SM6.6+ features (8-bit/16-bit packed dot products, atomic float operations, sampler feedback intrinsics) have no direct MSL equivalent or require Metal 3.x; older iPad GPUs (A13 and earlier) lack these.

wave_lane_size_mismatch: HLSL wave size is 32 on NVIDIA, 64 on AMD RDNA; MSL simdgroup is 32 on Apple GPUs. Algorithms that hardcode wave size break; the translation must rewrite to thread-position-in-simdgroup.
uav_atomic_subset: HLSL RWBuffer<float>::InterlockedAdd works on float since SM6.6; MSL float atomics require Metal 3.0+. Older iPads need a int-bitcast fallback.
register_packing_pitfalls: HLSL packoffset and register packing rules can produce non-portable cbuffer layouts that don't survive translation; sources should use explicit packoffset.
geometry_shader_unsupported: HLSL geometry shaders have no MSL equivalent; must be rewritten as compute + mesh, or removed.

no_runtime_compile_implementation_yet: the cross-compile pipeline (DXIL parse -> SPIR-V emit -> MSL emit, or direct DXIL -> MSL) is declared but not implemented in the substrate as runnable code; redefinition is symbolic.

name: redef_hlsl_to_msl
rationale: Demonstrates the per-shader-stage translation needed inside redef_d3d12_to_metal. This card lets ER's shader corpus be reasoned about at the cross-compile boundary.

source_form: win32_file_api(args...)
statement: For every win32 file API f in {CloseHandle, CopyFileW, CreateFileW, FlushFileBuffers, GetFileAttributesW, GetFileSize, MoveFileW, ReadFile, SetFilePointer, WriteFile}, the substrate has OBSERVED that calling f is sound-translatable to the POSIX call posix(f) per the table { CloseHandle -> close; CopyFileW -> sendfile; CreateFileW -> open; FlushFileBuffers -> fsync; GetFileAttributesW -> stat; GetFileSize -> fstat; MoveFileW -> rename; ReadFile -> read; SetFilePointer -> lseek; WriteFile -> write }. Witness: 10 agreeing observations + oracle.
target_form: posix(win32_file_api)(args...)
tentative_reason: Learned by the substrate's O1->O5 cycle against a synthetic 10-entry corpus with pre-known oracle (W53 proof-of-life). condition: OBSERVATIONALLY EQUIVALENT on the returned SEQUENCE iff: (a) underlying ordering is total and stable (typically sort by created_at + tie-break by id), (b) the dataset does not change between page fetches (or, with cursors: changes only at the tail). name: rest_pagination_offset_to_cursor
notes: Standard upgrade for any large feed API. Twitter, Stripe, GitHub, Slack all use cursor pagination. Cost: lose random-access ('jump to page 47'), gain insert-stability + O(log N) page-depth performance. The rewrite is LOSSY in capability (no jump) but more correct under concurrent writes. Combined sort key + tie-breaker is the load-bearing precondition (e.g. (created_at DESC, id DESC) — id makes total).
source_form:
# Offset pagination: client requests page N
GET /items?limit=20&offset=40        # rows 41-60
# Server query:
SELECT * FROM items ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40;
# Problem 1: DB must skip 40 rows -- O(N) cost grows with offset (deep pagination is slow)
# Problem 2: if rows inserted between client's page 2 and page 3 fetch, items shift; client sees duplicates or skips
target_form:
# Cursor pagination: client passes the last-seen key
GET /items?limit=20                              # first page
# response: { items: [...], next_cursor: 'eyJpZCI6NjB9' }
GET /items?limit=20&cursor=eyJpZCI6NjB9          # next page
# Server query: cursor decodes to last_id=60
SELECT * FROM items WHERE id > 60 ORDER BY id LIMIT 20;
# - O(log N) seek (index lookup) regardless of page depth
# - Stable under inserts: client continues from id=60 always

condition: MATHEMATICALLY EXACT at the information-content level — a single isolated log line carries strictly LESS information than the same log line annotated with a request-scoped correlation_id (and optionally span_id, parent_span_id). The rewrite is INFORMATION-ENRICHING: every log line gains the ability to be joined with every other log line from the same logical request, across processes and services. Equivalence requires: (a) correlation_id is propagated through every async/RPC boundary (via HTTP header X-Request-ID / traceparent, message envelopes, thread/asyncio context), (b) all logging sites read the active correlation_id from the runtime context, (c) the ID is unique enough (UUID or 64-bit random). LOSSY when: legacy services / third-party libraries don't propagate the header, breaking the chain; logs are emitted before request context is established (boot/shutdown).

name: single_log_to_correlation_id_trace
notes: Single most valuable observability upgrade for distributed systems. Costs almost nothing per log line (one extra field) but transforms debug experience. The rewrite has TWO load-bearing requirements: (1) propagation across every boundary (thread, asyncio, HTTP, MQ), (2) ALL log sites pull from the context. Failing either leaves a broken trace. OpenTelemetry's traceparent is the standard form (W3C); ad-hoc X-Request-ID is the historical form. This card is the entry point to the next card (opentelemetry_spans_replacing_callgraph_trace).
source_form:
# Plain logs — each line stands alone, hard to correlate across services
import logging
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def handle_order(order):
    log.info('order received id=%s', order.id)
    inventory.reserve(order.items)        # logs inside inventory: no link back to this order
    payment.charge(order.amount)          # logs inside payment: no link
    log.info('order completed id=%s', order.id)
# To debug a slow order, you must grep across services for 'order.id=42' — only works if every log line
# happens to mention order.id. Internal helper logs are orphaned.
target_form:
# Correlation-ID / trace propagation
import logging, uuid, contextvars
request_id_var = contextvars.ContextVar('request_id', default='-')

class ContextFilter(logging.Filter):
    def filter(self, record):
        record.request_id = request_id_var.get()
        return True

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
log.addFilter(ContextFilter())   # every record gets request_id field

def handle_order(order, incoming_request_id=None):
    rid = incoming_request_id or str(uuid.uuid4())
    token = request_id_var.set(rid)
    try:
        log.info('order received id=%s', order.id)        # auto-includes request_id
        with rpc_headers({'X-Request-ID': rid}):
            inventory.reserve(order.items)                # downstream service propagates rid
            payment.charge(order.amount)
        log.info('order completed id=%s', order.id)
    finally:
        request_id_var.reset(token)
# Every log line in this request — local AND downstream — shares request_id=rid

It proved redefinitions can DUPLICATE an existing input surface (a second paddle controlled by port 1). That demonstration is necessary but not sufficient — duplicating a handler is a near-trivial AST splice. The SECOND redefinition demo (this card) is required to prove the mechanism can also ADD GENUINELY NEW LOGIC: new state fields whose semantics did not exist anywhere in the source (the AI snake body + AI direction + score_p2 + done_p2), new helper functions encoding new behavior (greedy AI policy, mirrored advance step, cross-snake collision checks), and new control flow inside tick() that conditionally fires on the new game-over condition. The smoke's bit-identical-player-kernel assertion (with AI parked) is the L41 evidence that this redefinition extended the card additively rather than secretly rewriting the player snake logic. The substrate does NOT synthesize the AI policy — the policy is hand-coded inside _ai_compute_direction; the substrate mechanically and deterministically inserts that policy into the existing card while preserving the player kernel bit-identically. This honest scope is documented in cards/redefinition/snake_ai_opponent/python.py and in the wave 13 integration audit.
statement: Mechanically transform cards/example/snake_single_player/python.py into Snake + greedy AI opponent by AST-level edits: insert snake2_x_0..31 / snake2_y_0..31 / snake2_len / snake2_dir_x / snake2_dir_y / score_p2 / done_p2 into init_state; insert helper functions _get_snake2_x / _get_snake2_y / _set_snake2_cell / _ai_compute_direction / _advance_ai_snake; replace tick() with a new body that runs both the player branch (under the renamed done_p1) and, on the same FRAMES_PER_STEP gate, the AI direction-compute + advance; replace is_done() with a both-dead predicate; insert AI body rect appends into render_primitives() under a new COLOR_AI constant; rename state['score']->state['score_p1'] and state['done']->state['done_p1'] in the original _advance_snake body. The python.py in this card exposes apply(source_card_path, output_card_path) that performs the transform deterministically; the smoke verifies the produced module's PLAYER kernel is bit-identical to the source under zero input (with AI disabled), the AI logic actually fires (>=5 unique cells, >=2 unique directions) with AI enabled, and that a player suicide does NOT end the game while the AI is still alive.

condition: MATHEMATICALLY EXACT: softmax(x) = exp(x)/sum(exp(x)) = exp(x - max(x))/sum(exp(x - max(x))) because the max factor cancels in numerator and denominator. The rewrite is numerically NON-LOSSY in finite-precision float — it strictly improves stability by avoiding overflow when any x_i > log(MAX_FLOAT) ~ 88.7 for f32. Equivalence holds for all finite input; the only difference is that the naive form returns NaN/Inf for large inputs while the stable form does not. Caller must accept that 'naive overflows -> stable gives correct softmax' is the intended improvement, not a bug.

examples.note: happy path: small values; both forms numerically identical to ~6 decimal places
the WHOLE POINT: naive form is broken for large inputs (common in attention logits); stable form correct
underflow case also fixed by max-subtract

condition: An explicit finite state machine (states S, transition table T : S x Event -> S, actions) is observationally equivalent to a single actor (Erlang/Akka/Elixir/Pony) whose recursive receive loop encodes the same states and message-driven transitions. Both produce identical event-trace -> state-trace mappings on the same input sequence. The rewrite is DIRECT for single-entity workloads: an FSM transition is exactly an actor 'receive Event -> become(new_state)'. Both serialize concurrent events through a single locus (queue or transition step). The rewrite extends naturally to multi-entity by replicating actors; the converse (multi-actor system -> single FSM) requires composing the FSMs into a product machine and is exponential in actor count.

name: state_machine_explicit_to_actor_model
notes: Hewitt's actor model (1973) and finite automata (Mealy/Moore machines, McCulloch-Pitts 1943) are formally related: an actor that ignores aliasing and only changes its 'become' state in response to messages IS a Mealy machine where messages are inputs and outputs are reply messages. The rewrite is direct for single-entity systems. Erlang's 'gen_statem' OTP behaviour explicitly implements FSMs as actors. For multi-entity composition the actor model wins on scalability (no exponential blowup of explicit product FSM); for verification, the explicit FSM is easier to model-check. cost_score 25 reflects the syntactic translation cost; semantic preservation is exact.

condition: POINT-ESTIMATE EQUIVALENCE under uniform (improper or proper-bounded) prior: argmax_theta p(theta | data) = argmax_theta p(data | theta) when p(theta) is constant on the parameter space. So the Bayesian MAP estimate EQUALS the frequentist MLE. The full POSTERIOR is not equal to anything frequentist — it carries uncertainty information the MLE discards — but the MODE of the posterior coincides with the MLE. Caveats: (1) uniform prior on theta is NOT invariant under reparametrization, so MAP_theta != MAP_phi(theta) in general; MLE has the same invariance only by definition (MLE_g = g(MLE_theta) for any 1-1 g, while MAP changes under nonlinear g due to Jacobian). (2) The credible interval (Bayes) and confidence interval (frequentist) generally differ even under uniform prior. (3) For unbounded parameter spaces the uniform 'prior' is improper — the posterior may still be proper if the likelihood is integrable. Domain: any parametric model with well-defined likelihood.

examples.note: happy path: numerically identical point estimate (0.7000) — uniform prior contributes a flat additive constant to the log objective
examples.source_eval: MAP with Uniform(0,1) prior: posterior Beta(8,4) has mode = 7/10 = 0.70

examples.note: improper uniform: posterior still proper because likelihood is integrable in mu; MAP=MLE exactly
examples.source_eval: MAP with Uniform(-inf, inf) prior (improper): posterior is Gaussian, mean = sample mean = 1.10

input.model: Bernoulli(p) reparametrized via logit phi = log(p/(1-p))

examples.note: BIGGEST REPARAMETRIZATION TRADEOFF: uniform-prior MAP is NOT invariant — Jacobian |dp/dphi| = p(1-p) re-shapes the prior on p; MLE IS invariant by construction. Use Jeffreys prior 1/sqrt(p(1-p)) if you want a reparametrization-invariant Bayesian analog of MLE
examples.source_eval: MAP on phi with Uniform(phi): max of p^k(1-p)^(n-k) * |dp/dphi| = max of p^(k+1)(1-p)^(n-k+1), mode at (k+1)/(n+2) = 8/12 = 0.667
examples.target_eval: MLE on phi: phi_hat = logit(k/n) -> back-transforms to p_hat = 0.70

name: stats_bayes_to_frequentist_uniform_prior
notes: Common misconception: 'Bayesian with uniform prior = frequentist'. True for the point estimate, FALSE for uncertainty quantification and FALSE under reparametrization. The deeper equivalence is that MLE is the limit of MAP as the prior becomes less informative — but 'less informative' is parametrization-dependent. See stats_mle_to_map_uniform_prior for the direct algebraic statement.
source_form:
# Bayesian point estimate (MAP) with uniform prior
import numpy as np
def map_estimate_uniform_prior(log_likelihood, theta_grid):
    # prior is constant -> log posterior = log likelihood + const
    log_post = np.array([log_likelihood(t) for t in theta_grid])
    return theta_grid[np.argmax(log_post)]
# E.g. Binomial(n, p): p ~ Uniform(0,1); posterior is Beta(k+1, n-k+1); MAP = k/n
target_form:
# Frequentist MLE — direct maximization of the likelihood
import numpy as np
def mle(log_likelihood, theta_grid):
    log_lik = np.array([log_likelihood(t) for t in theta_grid])
    return theta_grid[np.argmax(log_lik)]
# E.g. Binomial(n, p): MLE p_hat = k/n (closed form: d/dp [k log p + (n-k) log(1-p)] = 0)

condition: BIAS-ESTIMATE EQUIVALENCE TO FIRST ORDER, DIFFERENT VARIANCE: both bootstrap (Efron 1979) and jackknife (Quenouille 1949, Tukey 1958) estimate the same quantities — bias and standard error of an estimator T(x_1,...,x_n) — using only the observed sample. For SMOOTH statistics (mean, variance, regression coefficients, smooth functionals of empirical CDF) both methods agree to O(1/n) on bias and standard error: bootstrap_bias = (B-1)/B * jackknife_bias + O(1/n). They are EXACTLY equal for the sample mean: jackknife and bootstrap (in the limit B->inf) both give SE = sigma_hat/sqrt(n). For NON-smooth statistics (median, quantiles, max) jackknife is INCONSISTENT — its SE estimate does not converge to the true SE — while bootstrap remains consistent. Variance characteristic: jackknife uses only n leave-one-out estimates, so its variance estimate has lower simulation variance for fixed compute but cannot capture higher-order moments; bootstrap with B=1000+ resamples captures the full sampling distribution including skew and kurtosis but is monte-carlo noisy. Domain: any plug-in estimator T(F_n) where F_n is the empirical CDF.

examples.note: happy path: smooth statistic, perfect agreement; jackknife gives EXACT zero bias for the sample mean by construction
smooth functional; both methods agree to 2 significant figures; jackknife is cheaper (50 evals vs 2000)

BIGGEST NON-SMOOTH FAILURE: jackknife is INCONSISTENT for the median, quantiles, and maximum. Use 'delete-d jackknife' with d/sqrt(n) -> inf to fix this, but at that point you might as well bootstrap. Bootstrap dominates for non-smooth statistics
examples.source_eval: Bootstrap (B=2000): SE_hat ~ 0.176 (matches asymptotic SE = 1/(2 f(median) sqrt(n)) ~ 0.177)
examples.target_eval: Jackknife: SE_hat ~ 0.103, INCONSISTENT — Efron-Stein bound shows jackknife SE for the median converges to wrong value because removing one point can shift the median by zero (no change) or by O(1/n) (jumps), violating the smoothness assumption

name: stats_bootstrap_to_jackknife
notes: Efron (1979): 'The bootstrap is to the jackknife as the Taylor series is to the linear approximation.' The jackknife is a first-order Taylor expansion of the bootstrap around the observed sample — exact when the statistic is linear, inconsistent when the statistic has discontinuities. For smooth estimators they are interchangeable; choose jackknife when n is small and stat() is expensive (n evaluations), choose bootstrap when stat() is cheap and the sampling distribution may be skewed.
source_form:
# Bootstrap: B resamples with replacement
import numpy as np
def bootstrap_bias_se(x, stat, B=1000):
    n = len(x)
    theta_hat = stat(x)
    theta_boot = np.array([stat(np.random.choice(x, n, replace=True)) for _ in range(B)])
    bias_hat = np.mean(theta_boot) - theta_hat
    se_hat = np.std(theta_boot, ddof=1)
    return bias_hat, se_hat
target_form:
# Jackknife: n leave-one-out estimates
import numpy as np
def jackknife_bias_se(x, stat):
    n = len(x)
    theta_hat = stat(x)
    theta_loo = np.array([stat(np.delete(x, i)) for i in range(n)])
    theta_bar = np.mean(theta_loo)
    bias_hat = (n - 1) * (theta_bar - theta_hat)
    se_hat = np.sqrt((n - 1) / n * np.sum((theta_loo - theta_bar)**2))
    return bias_hat, se_hat

condition: EXACT DISTRIBUTIONAL EQUALITY: Chi-squared(k) = Gamma(shape = k/2, scale = 2). Density of Chi-squared(k): f(x) = x^(k/2 - 1) exp(-x/2) / (2^(k/2) Gamma(k/2)) for x > 0. Density of Gamma(alpha, theta) with shape alpha and scale theta: f(x) = x^(alpha-1) exp(-x/theta) / (theta^alpha Gamma(alpha)). Substituting alpha = k/2 and theta = 2 makes the densities identical. So sampling, CDF, moments, MGF all coincide. Caveat: there are TWO common Gamma parametrizations: (shape alpha, scale theta) vs (shape alpha, rate beta = 1/theta). Under rate parameterization: Chi-squared(k) = Gamma(shape = k/2, rate = 1/2). Mismatch between scipy.stats.gamma (uses scale) and many statistics texts (use rate) is the #1 bug. Domain: k >= 1 integer for chi-squared from a normal SS; the Gamma generalization works for any continuous alpha > 0, so this also defines 'fractional chi-squared'.

notes: Practical use: Chi-squared(k) being Gamma(k/2, scale=2) means (a) confidence intervals for variances via Chi-squared are Gamma quantiles, (b) the Wishart distribution (matrix Chi-squared) generalizes via matrix Gamma, (c) the non-central Chi-squared has no clean Gamma form — it is its own distribution. The factor 2 in scale comes from the 1/sqrt(2*pi) and 1/2 in the standard-normal density.
source_form:
# Chi-squared(k) via sum of squared standard normals
import numpy as np
def sample_chi_squared(k, n_samples=1):
    # X ~ Chi-squared(k) <=> X = sum_{i=1}^{k} Z_i^2, Z_i iid N(0,1)
    Z = np.random.randn(n_samples, k)
    return np.sum(Z**2, axis=1)

condition: DIRECT ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY: KL(p || q) = H(p, q) - H(p), where H(p, q) = -sum_x p(x) log q(x) is the cross-entropy and H(p) = -sum_x p(x) log p(x) is the entropy of p. Equivalent form: H(p, q) = H(p) + KL(p || q). Consequence: when p is FIXED (e.g., empirical training distribution), minimizing KL(p || q) over q is EQUIVALENT to minimizing H(p, q) because H(p) is constant. This is why classification networks train on cross-entropy loss but are equivalently maximum-likelihood (= minimum KL) learners. The equivalence requires support(p) subset of support(q); if p(x) > 0 but q(x) = 0 for some x then KL = +infinity. Symmetry: KL is NOT symmetric (KL(p||q) != KL(q||p)); cross-entropy H(p,q) is also not symmetric. The 'symmetrized KL' (Jeffreys divergence) and Jensen-Shannon divergence are separate constructions. Domain: discrete or continuous probability distributions over the same measurable space; densities replace probabilities in the integrand.

this is why 'softmax + cross-entropy loss' = 'softmax + negative log likelihood' = 'minimum KL to the empirical distribution' — three names for the same gradient

name: stats_kl_divergence_to_cross_entropy
notes: Foundational identity for machine learning: cross-entropy loss is THE go-to classification objective because (a) when the label distribution p is fixed (one-hot or smoothed) the constant H(p) drops out under argmin, (b) gradient w.r.t. softmax logits is the clean (q - p) form, (c) it generalizes seamlessly to soft labels and knowledge distillation. The forward KL(p||q) is 'mode-covering' (penalizes q for missing support of p); reverse KL(q||p) is 'mode-seeking' (used in variational inference).
target_form:
# Cross-entropy minus entropy of p
import numpy as np
def kl_via_cross_entropy(p, q, eps=1e-12):
    p = np.asarray(p) + eps
    q = np.asarray(q) + eps
    H_pq = -np.sum(p * np.log(q))     # cross-entropy
    H_p  = -np.sum(p * np.log(p))     # entropy of p
    return H_pq - H_p

condition: TARGET-DISTRIBUTION EQUIVALENCE: both Metropolis-Hastings (MH) and Gibbs sampling produce Markov chains whose stationary distribution is the joint posterior pi(theta_1, ..., theta_d | data). Special case: Gibbs sampling IS Metropolis-Hastings with proposal distribution q(theta_i' | theta_-i) = pi(theta_i | theta_-i, data) (the full conditional). With this proposal the MH acceptance ratio reduces algebraically to 1, so EVERY proposal is accepted — Gibbs is 'Metropolis with 100% acceptance'. Strong equivalence holds when the model has conjugate priors so the full conditionals are known and samplable in closed form (Normal-Inverse-Gamma, Beta-Binomial, Dirichlet-Multinomial). Outside conjugacy: Gibbs requires a numerical sampler for each conditional (Adaptive Rejection Sampling, slice sampling) or degenerates to Metropolis-within-Gibbs. Convergence (TVD to stationarity, autocorrelation time) is generally BETTER for Gibbs in conjugate models because there is no rejection waste, but WORSE when components are highly correlated (Gibbs moves only along axes; MH with multivariate proposal can move diagonally). Domain: any joint distribution with computable conditional densities.

examples.target_eval: Gibbs: mean(mu_chain)~2.02, mean(sigma^2_chain)~2.31, acceptance rate = 1.00, ESS ~ 4900 (nearly iid)

name: stats_mcmc_metropolis_to_gibbs
notes: Folklore: 'Gibbs is just MH with acceptance 1.' True algebraically: q(theta_i'|theta_-i) = pi(theta_i'|theta_-i) makes the MH ratio pi(theta')*q(theta|theta') / (pi(theta)*q(theta'|theta)) = pi(theta_i'|theta_-i)*pi(theta_-i)*pi(theta_i|theta_-i) / (pi(theta_i|theta_-i)*pi(theta_-i)*pi(theta_i'|theta_-i)) = 1. The practical equivalence requires conjugacy or another way to sample the conditionals. For non-conjugate models people use Metropolis-within-Gibbs (MH update inside each conditional step) which is again MH — just structured.
source_form:
# Metropolis-Hastings — generic, works without conjugacy
import numpy as np
def metropolis_hastings(log_target, theta0, n_iter, proposal_sd=0.5):
    theta = np.array(theta0, dtype=float)
    chain = np.zeros((n_iter, len(theta)))
    log_p = log_target(theta)
    for t in range(n_iter):
        theta_prop = theta + np.random.randn(len(theta)) * proposal_sd
        log_p_prop = log_target(theta_prop)
        if np.log(np.random.rand()) < log_p_prop - log_p:
            theta, log_p = theta_prop, log_p_prop      # accept
        chain[t] = theta
    return chain
target_form:
# Gibbs sampling under conjugate priors — sample each conditional in closed form
import numpy as np
def gibbs_normal_inv_gamma(y, n_iter):
    # Conjugate model: y_i ~ N(mu, sigma^2); mu | sigma^2 ~ N(0, sigma^2/k0); sigma^2 ~ InvGamma(a,b)
    n = len(y); ybar = np.mean(y); k0 = 0.01; a0 = 1.0; b0 = 1.0
    mu = ybar; sigma2 = np.var(y)
    chain = np.zeros((n_iter, 2))
    for t in range(n_iter):
        kn = k0 + n
        mu = np.random.normal((k0*0 + n*ybar)/kn, np.sqrt(sigma2/kn))               # full conditional of mu
        an = a0 + n/2; bn = b0 + 0.5*np.sum((y - mu)**2) + 0.5*k0*mu**2
        sigma2 = 1.0 / np.random.gamma(an, 1/bn)                                      # full conditional of sigma^2
        chain[t] = [mu, sigma2]
    return chain

condition: DIRECT ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY: for any parametric model with likelihood L(theta) = p(data | theta), MAP_theta = argmax p(theta | data) with prior pi(theta) = const equals argmax L(theta) = MLE_theta. Proof: log p(theta|data) = log L(theta) + log pi(theta) - log p(data); the second term is constant in theta and the third does not depend on theta, so argmax is preserved. This is parameterization-fixed: it holds *for the specific theta-coordinates in which the prior is uniform*. Under reparametrization phi = g(theta), the uniform prior on theta induces prior |dg^-1/dphi| on phi, so MAP_phi != g(MAP_theta) for nonlinear g. MLE IS reparametrization-invariant: argmax L(theta) under theta = g^-1(phi) is g(argmax L(g^-1(phi))). Domain: any model where the likelihood has a well-defined maximum; the prior can be improper (constant on unbounded space) provided the posterior is proper.

def mle(neg_log_lik, theta_init):

# MAP with uniform prior — algebraically identical objective
import numpy as np
def map_uniform(neg_log_lik, theta_init):
    from scipy.optimize import minimize
    # log prior is a constant -> drops out of argmax
    neg_log_post = lambda t: neg_log_lik(t) + 0.0
    res = minimize(neg_log_post, theta_init)
    return res.x
# By construction map_uniform == mle for the same neg_log_lik and theta_init

condition: ASYMPTOTIC EQUIVALENCE (de Moivre-Laplace, special case of CLT): Binomial(n, p) converges in distribution to Normal(np, np(1-p)) as n -> infinity with p in (0,1) fixed. Formally: (X - np) / sqrt(np(1-p)) -d-> N(0,1). The approximation is *good* when np >= 5 and n(1-p) >= 5 (rule of thumb); the error in CDF is O(1/sqrt(n)) by Berry-Esseen. NOT equivalent for fixed n (binomial is discrete with finite support [0,n]; normal is continuous on R), so the rewrite swaps a discrete PMF for a continuous PDF + continuity correction P(X <= k) ~ Phi((k+0.5-np)/sqrt(np(1-p))). Breaks down at the tails (large deviations) — use Chernoff/Poisson there. Domain: any X = sum of n iid Bernoulli(p) trials.

small np=2 violates rule of thumb; ~1.2% absolute error; Poisson(2) approx gives 0.9473 (closer for this regime)
BIGGEST TAIL FAILURE: normal underestimates tail by ~60% at 6-sigma; for large deviations use Chernoff/large-deviations not CLT — CLT is a CENTRAL limit, not a tail tool
